featured_reviews.name: Sagar Abichandani
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Hinglaj (Hingla/Hinglay) Devi Mandir, Versova (Andheri West), Mumbai | Powerful Shakti Darshan in Versova Koliwada

If you’re searching for a deeply devotional Devi mandir in Versova, Hinglaj Devi Mandir (Patil Galli / Pandurang Ramle Marg, Versova, Andheri West) is a place that genuinely feels charged with Shakti. As a staunch Hindu believer, my darshan here felt profoundly grounding—calm on the surface, yet spiritually powerful from within.  ￼

🛕 What makes this mandir special (specifics, not generic praise)

This temple is dedicated to Maa Hinglaj (Hinglaj Devi)—an aspect of Goddess Durga/Shakti who is widely revered across India, and whose principal pilgrimage shrine is the famous Hinglaj Mata Temple (also called Nani Mandir) in Balochistan. Knowing this spiritual lineage adds depth to the experience—especially for devotees who connect strongly with Shakti worship.  ￼

📍 Location clarity (very easy to find)

The mandir is located in Versova Village / Versova Koliwada, in the Patil Galli lane off Pandurang Ramle Marg (Mumbai 400061). It’s one of those temples that locals know well, and it’s straightforward to reach by auto/cab once you’re in Versova.  ￼

⏰ Timings (practical, devotee-friendly)

Most reliable local listings show it is typically open daily from ~7:00 AM to 10:00 PM (some listings show “open until 10 PM” as well). This makes it very convenient for working professionals who want evening darshan.  ￼

🙏 Darshan experience & “energy” of the place

The sanctum area feels focused and devotional—no unnecessary noise, no distraction—just a steady spiritual atmosphere that helps you pray with attention. Even on a busy day, the overall vibe stays respectful, and you can feel why so many devotees come here regularly, especially during auspicious periods.

🌺 Festivals & crowd expectations

During Navratri and other Devi occasions, Versova’s devotional energy rises and crowds naturally increase—so I recommend coming early morning for a quieter, more meditative darshan, or late evening if you prefer a calmer flow. (Temple reels and local posts frequently show Navratri celebrations and devotee footfall here.)  ￼

🧼 Cleanliness & management

For a neighborhood temple with steady footfall, the space is generally maintained well, and the darshan flow remains manageable. It’s the kind of place where the devotion feels sincere and community-rooted.

⸻

⭐ Final verdict: 5/5

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Five stars for spiritual connect, Shakti presence, and a genuinely uplifting darshan experience in Versova.
If you’re looking up “Hinglaj Devi Mandir Versova,” “Hingla Devi temple Andheri West,” or simply want a powerful Devi darshan in Mumbai’s western suburbs—this temple is absolutely worth visiting.

🙏 Jai Maa Hinglaj Devi 🙏

featured_reviews.review_text: Visiting Shiv Ganesh Mandir was a beautiful and peaceful experience. The divine presence of Lord Shiva and Lord Ganesha fills the temple with positive and calming energy. The aarti was soulful and heart-touching. A wonderful place to pray, seek blessings, and feel spiritually uplifted.

featured_reviews.name: Travel Photographer
featured_reviews.review_text: Beautiful Temple located in 1st cross lane of Lokhandwala Market. Every day people from Lokhandwala and other neighbouring localities comes here for peaceful darshan. Idols of Lord Ganesh ,  Lord Hanuman and Lord Shiva are nicely  placed in this temple. Temple premises are very neat and clean. You can feed grass to cows here. This temple  occasionally organizes medical camps in the premises.  Management is very polite and helpful for devotees. Very limited parking facility is provided by the temple for all types of vehicles.

customer_updates.text:
Our Gurudwara Sahib ji always tries to keep our mother earth 🌍 clean during Gurpurab when sangat is more they get Pattal plate which is made from dried leaves  ,offering a biodegradable alternative to plastic.
The sangat puts all these pattal  in the dustbin as it gets full of plastic bags. These bags are removed from dustbins new bags are placed..
When ever you organise kirtan at your  home please 🙏 used pattal inside of thermocol plates
We used  steel plates ,steel spoons,& steel glass every Sunday & support substabilty..
Avoid using plastic.

customer_updates.name: Rosy Kohli
customer_updates.text:
Celebrating 552nd GURPURAB
SAHIB SRI GURU NANAK DEV JI, after lockdown today we celebrate the Prakash Purab, due to pandemic no one was allowed to go to Gurdware only people staying there inside would do prayers. But Langer( food) was made daily was served twice afternoon & night in lockdown . Taking all safety precautions food packets were given my tailor told me as no work, due to lockdown he used have food here every day, near by people staying in slum would come,take langar packets auto wala today told me mam there no passenger people were not moving in out in lockdown,it was difficult, but we got food from Sikh Gurdware, they serve us with smile face we used stand in queue wearing mask . I said yes most of Gurdware in Mumbai served langar
Today felt happy after years we got to celebrate with Grace of God all program went smoothly. Some were wearing mask some removed when entered inside . But I took all safety measures wore mask, during the whole program,had Langar left.And prayed 🙏to babaji bless everyone is safe and we living normal life.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Every Sunday here we go to Gurudwara here we listen to kirtan they around 12.40-2.30pm langar( food) is served to everyone, whether he rich or poor all sit together with there head covered have food,even outside the Gurudwara food is given to people near by .
When people come should always cover there head & should have tabacco,drink, smokers are not allowed inside then such people who come from slums are give food outside the Gurudwara.
When we Gurupurab then special arrangements are made people from different area come together celebrate,give contribution also as per there wish.
Now even at night they serve food .This they started few months back.

It's easily seen from road. There is no parking available in front of gurudwara.
Accessible till main gate ♿ then step is there. Yes gurudwara volunteers will help you inside but when u seek darshan inside the gurudwara wheel chair is not allowed. .
Due due pandemic crowd is not allowed.
Wearing mask is Compulsory .

customer_updates.name: Rosy Kohli
customer_updates.text:
Verosava Koli Sea Food Festival 2026 was absolutely wow! 😋
The main attraction was the fish stalls by the Koli community—fresh Surmai, Rawas, Pomfret, Prawns, Crab, cooked live with love. The Koli families were dressed in authentic traditional attire with beautiful gold jewellery, adding cultural charm.
Apart from seafood, there were momos, ice-cream, pani stall, waffle stalls, and food options for kids too.
Local dance performances on stage created a festive vibe 🩰
Many local leaders and celebrities visited; banners were displayed.
Good arrangements with tables, chairs, water, cold drinks, and clear washroom directions. The place is easily accessible.
Loved clicking photos with the performers and stalls 📸
A must-visit festival for seafood lovers and culture enthusiasts!
#Spottedonshorts.

featured_reviews.name: Poulami Basak
featured_reviews.review_text: Visited this place for Koli festival. This festival is surely a must watch visit if you are in Mumbai. You will get to taste various type of sea foods here. There r N number of shops, managed by the koli community people.All are offering you a large various of fish like Surmai, Bombil, Rawas, Tuna, Pomfret fry, Shells, Lobster, prawns, crabs and many more. You have to bargain with them to get the fried fishes at a good deal. There are tables and chairs to sit and enjoy the food. All the ladies of koli community are decked up with beautiful sarees and jewelleries. There was a arrangement of cultural program too which elevated the festival to a higher level.

featured_reviews.name: Abhijeet Khedgikar
featured_reviews.review_text:
This is Versova Fish Festival 2020, Its just next to the fishing village in Versova.  There were so many stall of sea food here and so many people. Every stall  is selling almost identical food, but still there was crowd at each and every stall. The sea food was of good quality but I might say, that the cost was a bit high. Almost every variety was available here. We tried the Lobster, Stuffed Pomfret , Surmai and crabs. The taste was exactly the same in all the stalls. There were cultural programs going on the stage centrally located. All in all, it was a wonderful one time experience.
To reach, take a metro to the last station Versova, and take an auto to the Ganesh temple or shiv Galli . Its close to versova metro Station , around 2 kms on foot.
